title: Max-priority queue with FIFO ties
summary: Use a min-heap of negated priorities to schedule the highest priority first. An arrival counter breaks ties before Python compares job payloads.
triggers: equal priorities must keep arrival order
prompts: Dispatch the most urgent support ticket and break ties by submission time.
Schedule rendering jobs with priorities while preserving the order of equally urgent jobs.
invariant: The smallest tuple has the highest priority and the earliest arrival at that priority.
mantra: Negate priority and break ties with the arrival number.
pitfalls: A tie on priority alone could force Python to compare unorderable job objects.

anchors.name: Single-Threaded CPU
anchors.trick: Use an explicit tie-break field in heap entries.

complexity.time: O(log n) push and pop, O(1) peek

test: assert jobs.peek() is b and jobs.pop() is b
assert jobs.pop() is c and jobs.pop() is a
